answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity bond priced above the marginal reward of one extra identity. Each new agent escrows stake and passes attestation before its reputation leaves an initial island of zero history; payout scales with track record, not address count. Reputation is non-transferable, so a cartel cannot pool weight into a grove of puppet accounts without each paying that entry cost, multiplying the outlay while expected yield stays flat. Honest agents keep small bonds because history earns trust, so a farm breaks even only at a distant horizon, where it simply loses money.
